answer_1.quote: We measure their performance on the SPRP task, prompting the models to generate split and rephrase hypotheses from complex sentences.
answer_1.outputs: Sequences of shorter sentences that preserve the meaning of the original complex sentence (split and rephrase).

answer_2.quote: we used three separate metrics to evaluate our models. SARI ..., the normalised BertScore (BESC) ..., BLEU scores ...; we also included an additional metric for the task to indicate output compliance (CPL).

answer_4.quote: human evaluators were presented a source sentence and two SPRP hypotheses, which they had to rank in a 3-way evaluation... 11 evaluators... We also performed an additional human evaluation... 8 human evaluators... answering six questions related to sensicality, grammaticality, missed facts, new facts, correct split and sufficient split.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators compared hypotheses according to compliance, sensicality, grammaticality, missed facts and omitted facts (3‑way ranking); in the qualitative study they answered six specific questions about sensicality, grammaticality, missing facts, new facts, correct split and enough split.
